plan: [Third-price auction (3 bidders): if I win I pay the lowest other bid, so my bid mainly controls winning. With no history and independent draws, bidding my true value ($25) is a robust, long-run-safe choice: I win when the opponents' minimum bid is below 25 and earn positive surplus, while avoiding systematic overpayment when opponent lows exceed my value.]

[Third-price with 3 bidders: the winner pays the lowest opponent bid, so payment doesn't depend on our bid if we win. Assuming opponents bid their values (reasonable baseline with no history), maximize E[(v - min(other bids)) * P(win)]. For uniform[0,49] opponents, this gives an interior optimum b = 2v. With my value v=3, bid 2*v = $6 to balance win probability and expected payment. ]

[With 3 bidders the winner pays the lowest bid. If I bid my true value ($26) then whenever I win I pay ≤26, so I cannot incur a loss. Overbidding raises win probability but risks paying more than my value if both opponents bid between 26 and my higher bid. No prior history to exploit, so bid my value to maximize long-run expected profit safely.]
